stories.headline: DeepSeek Suffers 12-Hour Outage Affecting 355M+ Users, Longest Downtime Since Debut

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek's chatbot went offline Sunday evening (March 29) and was not fully restored until Monday morning (March 30), totaling approximately 12 hours of downtime
key_facts.excerpt: Service went offline Sunday evening... fixes were implemented between 1am-9am Monday... Service restored by 9:13am Monday, officially marked 'resolved' at 10:33am

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek had over 355 million users as of February, making this outage one of the largest AI service disruptions to date
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek had over 355 million users as of February

key_facts.fact: Chinese social media was flooded with complaints, with one user saying: 'Only after DeepSeek went down did I realise I no longer knew how to work without it'
key_facts.excerpt: Only after DeepSeek went down did I realise I no longer knew how to work without it

key_facts.fact: Local rivals including Zhipu AI, MiniMax AI, and Moonshot AI have made major performance gains with their own releases, outshining DeepSeek
key_facts.excerpt: Local rivals including Zhipu AI, MiniMax AI, and Moonshot AI have 'made major performance gains with their own releases to global acclaim, outshining DeepSeek'

key_facts.fact: This was DeepSeek's second major disruption; the platform suffered denial-of-service attacks in late January following its R1 model release
key_facts.excerpt: This represents the second major service disruption; the platform experienced denial-of-service attacks in late January following its R1 model release
